Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. ## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Findings first, then two decisions for you.

**No conflict — you've found the one park with no resolver.**

- The janitor's Rule E (`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/janitor-rules.mjs:26`) *deliberately* excludes `approval` from `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS`, with the comment "an approval park typically holds an open PR". Rules A–F otherwise never touch a parked approval item. So nothing in the queue ever revisits one.
- The PR number is **already required** — `converge-item.mjs:54` refuses an approval converge without `--pr`. But it's only written as prose in the converge comment (`convergeComment`, `converge-item.mjs:88`: *"Waiting on a person: merge or close #133, then close this item"*). No parser can reach it. Your ask is therefore only **promoting a value we already hold into the machine block**, not gathering anything new.
- **`Blocked-by` can't carry it and won't collide.** `isReleasable` (`readiness.mjs:19`) requires `STATUS_BLOCKED`, so `Blocked-by` on a parked item is inert; and its semantics are "re-run when it closes", not "close when it closes". A new field is needed, and it doesn't clash with the deferred-request lane.
- It *resolves* an existing tension rather than creating one: our local rule forbids the delivered PR carrying `Closes #<item>` precisely because the native keyword overrides the intended park. A janitor rule reading the PR's state is the sanctioned replacement for that.
- **Second half nobody has flagged:** for a request-mode item, converge flips the origin issue to `claude-in-review` (`converge-item.mjs:141`). Whatever closes the item on merge must also clear that label, or every request issue keeps a stale in-review badge forever.
- **On the rename:** cheap mechanically — `LEGACY_STATUS` / `LEGACY_PARK_RE` / `spellingsOf` (`work-item.mjs:172-241`) is exactly the "written never, read forever" lane, and `convergeOps` already removes every spelling. The cost is elsewhere: `PARK_KINDS` and the `--outcome approval` CLI word appear in every `task.md`.

input.title: An approval park has no end condition — nothing closes it when its PR resolves
input.body:
A run that converges `--outcome approval` leaves the item **open** at `task:status:needs-human-approval`, with the PR number stated only in prose ("Waiting on a person: merge or close #133, then close this item").

Nothing ever revisits that. Rule E (the superseded park) deliberately excludes `approval` — an approval park holds an open PR, and a later clean run does not answer it — so once the PR merges, the item sits open forever until a person happens to read it and closes it by hand. The park states what a person owes, and no mechanism watches for that debt being paid.

## The change

A generic `Ends-when: #133 closed` field in the item's machine block, written by the converge for any park that names a `--pr`, plus a janitor rule that acts on it:

- merged → the work landed → `task:status:done`, closed `completed`
- closed unmerged → `task:status:rejected`, closed `not_planned`
- a marked issue is still never closed by the machinery — the terminal status stands on the open issue

Generic rather than approval-only so an action or decision park waiting on a setup issue can carry the same field, and so one rule reads it regardless of kind.

## Not a conflict with

- `Blocked-by` — `isReleasable` requires `task:status:blocked`, so a parked item carrying it is never released. That lane governs ready/blocked, not the end of a park.
- Rule E — complementary; this fills exactly the hole its exclusion of `approval` leaves.
- Rule F (orphaned park) — independent; both may claim an item, and superseded/orphaned already order among themselves.
- `Closes #<item>` in the PR body — explicitly forbidden already, because the native keyword overrides an intended park. This is the mechanism that replaces it.

Renaming `needs-human-approval` → `needs-pr-approval` is deliberately out of scope here.

## 11. Recovery — what the janitor keeps, what dies

| failure | today | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| scheduler/scheduler run miss or late fire | run-ledger catch-up math | same property from the occurrence guard (§5) — the next scheduler run instantiates the most recent occurrence only |
| double scheduler run | concurrency group + slot-title search | concurrency group + occurrence-guard search (same window, same answer) |
| lost label event | janitor re-arm (remove/re-add), 20-min grace, bounded by stale escalation | **retired** — executors poll on the scheduler run's cron; events are latency sugar, never the only delivery |
| duplicate events / racing executors | claim lease on one implicit executor | same lease, N executors — the loser picks a different item |
| executor died mid-claim | — (executor was a session; janitor reclaimed via `agent-running`) | **the scheduler run** (owner, 2026-08-13): `task:status:running-executor` with no activity past ~1h → strip to `task:status:waiting-for-executor` with a comment, so a dead executor's item is back in the queue within ~2h rather than ~25h. An executor iteration is minutes, not hours, and a lease checked once a day is not a short lease |
| executor run died with items still queued | n/a (one implicit executor; the next slot was a day away) | **the failure-continuation job** (owner, 2026-08-15): `needs: execute`, `if: failure() \|\| cancelled()` re-dispatches on a fresh runner, so the *queue* resumes in ~a minute while the dead run's own item waits for the leash; the scheduler run drain is the backstop when the whole workflow run is lost (§10, S36) |

| item never picked up | stale dispatch escalation, period parsed from the slot id's leading char | same escalation, period read from the task's declared `frequency` at HEAD (or a default for ad-hoc items) — no title parsing; the stale item converges `task:status:needs-human-action` — the lane is not being drained and the fix is outside the item — and leaves the queue |

The janitor remains an ordinary daily task and shrinks twice over: re-arm and
its grace window delete, and the **executing-leash reclaim moves to the scheduler run**
— a deterministic label rule, serialized and hourly, which is exactly the
scheduler run's kind of work. This amends the 2026-08-06 "all recovery lives in the
janitor" split, deliberately: the split's purpose was that recovery happen
*once, in one place, in code* rather than in every triggered session, and a
rule that runs once per scheduler run satisfies that as fully as one that runs once per
day. What stays with the janitor is everything needing judgment or a longer
horizon — four rules and a review: the dead *agent* claim (`task:status:running-agent`
silent past ~3h → `task:status:needs-human-decision` (what the dead
session left behind decides whether this re-queues), the hand-off comment naming which session
died), the stale-ready escalation (unpicked past ~2 periods →
a park), the stuck-dependency sweep (F14 above — comment-only), the
stateless-item repair (an open work item wearing neither a `task:*` state
nor a park — a torn label swap's leavings, §6.2 →
`task:status:needs-human-decision`),
and the health review, which gains the queue (ready-item age, blocked-item
depth, outcome mix) as its subject and can now compute all of it from
issues.

Two leash constraints, made explicit by the validation review (2026-08-13) and
the first **reframed by the work-as-work review (2026-08-15)**:

- **The executing leash measures executor death, never work duration — the
  heartbeat is what buys that (F17, reframed).** As first written, F17 made
  the leash exceed every task's work bound, which under the work-as-work model
  inflates it to the heaviest task in the fleet: one legitimate three-hour
  task and a dead executor on a two-minute task also waits three hours to
  reclaim. Instead the executor **comments a heartbeat on the item every ~15
  minutes during the work step** (§6.5): a live run is never reclaimed however
  long it works (S31c), a dead one stops heartbeating and is reclaimed within
  ~the leash of its last heartbeat regardless of the work's bound (S31d), and
  the wiring-time conformance check shrinks to the one relation the heartbeat
  itself needs — **heartbeat interval well inside the leash** (S31). The
  livelock the original constraint prevented — every tenure reclaimed alive
  before it can finish, the work re-executing forever, nothing converging —
  is still demonstrable by switching the heartbeat off (S31b), which is why
  the heartbeat is contract, not courtesy. The paired runtime rule is
  unchanged: an executor **re-verifies its own lease at every state
  transition** (is my claim still this episode's earliest?) and abandons
  silently when it is not — which is what keeps a reclaimed-but-alive runner
  from handing off work it no longer owns.

  within it** — parity with today's stale `agent-running` sweep, stated as
  an assumption rather than discovered as an incident: a legitimately

  clock, or it will be declared dead. (The same move as the executor's

input.body:
Closes #1468

An approval park leaves the item open holding an open pull request, with that PR named only in prose — "Waiting on a person: merge or close #133, then close this item". Nothing ever revisited it. Rule E (the superseded park) excludes the `approval` kind precisely because a later clean run does not answer a question about an open PR, so once the PR merged the item sat open until somebody happened to read it.

## What lands

**`Ends-when: #<n> closed`** — a machine-block field, stamped by the converge on **any** park given a `--pr` (required on `approval`, accepted on the rest). `#<n> closed` is its whole grammar: a condition the janitor cannot evaluate reads as absent, never as met.

**Janitor rule G, the ended park** — reads that target's resolution and ends the item accordingly:

| target | item |
|---|---|
| merged | `task:status:done`, closed `completed` — the work landed |
| closed unmerged | `task:status:rejected`, closed `not_planned` |
| open / unreadable | untouched — the park is the machinery working |

Reading merged-ness rather than state is the point: a park closed `rejected` when its PR in fact merged reports a delivered run as one that never happened. A marked issue takes the status and stays open — closing the person's own issue is still theirs (§16.5). A legacy shadow item's request issue gets its `claude-in-review` taken back, since nothing else ever would.

## Not a conflict with

- **`Blocked-by`** — `isReleasable` requires `task:status:blocked`, so a parked item carrying it is never released. That lane releases an item to *run again*; this one *ends* one that already ran.
- **Rule E** — complementary. It fills exactly the hole the `approval` exclusion leaves, and the exclusion's comment now says so.
- **Rules E and F** — an item they already claimed is skipped, as those two already order among themselves.
- **`Closes #<item>` in a PR body** — already forbidden, because the native keyword fires on merge and overrides an intended park. This is the mechanism that replaces it.

Renaming `needs-human-approval` → `needs-pr-approval` was considered and deliberately left out: it is a second concern, and the label is stored data on live items in every member.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/     the Ends-when field and its parse/stamp on work-item.mjs,

                                  session-script executors), and rule G in janitor-rules.mjs

                                  merged-ness and acts on rule G's verdict
packs/claudinite-tasks/           setIssueBody on github.mjs; the --pr guidance in the

packs/claudinite-growth/skills/   writing-tasks names the end condition beside the park it

docs/tasks-dispatch/              the item-body grammar and the §11 recovery table gain the

```

A park closed `rejected` when its PR actually merged reports a delivered run as one that never happened, so rule G reads `pull_request.merged_at`, not just state — merged → `done`/`completed`, closed → `rejected`/`not_planned`.

{"number":1472,"title":"A park can state what would end it, and the janitor closes it when it does","body":"Closes #1468

An approval park leaves the item open holding an open pull request, with that PR named only in prose — "Waiting on a person: merge or close #133, then close this item". Nothing ever revisited it. Rule E (the superseded park) excludes the `approval` kind precisely because a later clean run does not answer a question about an open PR, so once the PR merged the item sat open until somebody happened to read it.

## What lands

**`Ends-when: # closed`** — a machine-block field, stamped by the converge on **any** park given a `--pr` (required on `approval`, accepted on the rest). `# closed` is its whole grammar: a condition the janitor cannot evaluate reads as absent, never as met.

**Janitor rule G, the ended park** — reads that target's resolution and ends the item accordingly:

| target | item |
|---|---|
| merged | `task:status:done`, closed `completed` — the work landed |
| closed unmerged | `task:status:rejected`, closed `not_planned` |
| open / unreadable | untouched — the park is the machinery working |

Reading merged-ness rather than state is the point: a park closed `rejected` when its PR in fact merged reports a delivered run as one that never happened. A marked issue takes the status and stays open — closing the person's own issue is still theirs (§16.5). A legacy shadow item's request issue gets its `claude-in-review` taken back, since nothing else ever would.

## Not a conflict with

- **`Blocked-by`** — `isReleasable` requires `task:status:blocked`, so a parked item carrying it is never released. That lane releases an item to *run again*; this one *ends* one that already ran.
- **Rule E** — complementary. It fills exactly the hole the `approval` exclusion leaves, and the exclusion's comment now says so.
- **Rules E and F** — an item they already claimed is skipped, as those two already order among themselves.
- **`Closes #` in a PR body** — already forbidden, because the native keyword fires on merge and overrides an intended park. This is the mechanism that replaces it.

Renaming `needs-human-approval` → `needs-pr-approval` was considered and deliberately left out: it is a second concern, and the label is stored data on live items in every member.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/     the Ends-when field and its parse/stamp on work-item.mjs,
                                  the setBody op in convergeOps (both the REST and the
                                  session-script executors), and rule G in janitor-rules.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/     the janitor's queue sweep reads each Ends-when target's
                                  merged-ness and acts on rule G's verdict
packs/claudinite-tasks/           setIssueBody on github.mjs; the --pr guidance in the
                                  executor's queue instructions
packs/claudinite-growth/skills/   writing-tasks names the end condition beside the park it
                                  describes
docs/tasks-dispatch/              the item-body grammar and the §11 recovery table gain the
                                  row this closes
```

Verified: every new assertion watched to fail first (fencing accepted anything → 2 red; merged/closed collapsed and the marked-issue guard removed → 2 red; the stamp dropped → 4 red). # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,

   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
